title: Timeline of the show and Rhythm Red's song
summary: Green dates the Bert Wheeler run from 1966-67, then the Mercury; dancers drifted back to other commitments, Rhythm Red wrote Got to Go Tap Dancing Tonight, and they met Jack Bradley.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: When did you form the Chuck Green -- "Reminiscing with Chuck Green?"
Well, immediately after we returned from the tours. We --
And that lasted for a year in the Bert Wheeler Theater?
And then after that you moved into the Mercury Theater.
And that lasted for how long, another year?
Well, that went from like -- I would say from -- it went about a year and into its second year.

So, as a tap dancers got less and less, see, because now one of them had to go back to his school. He was a teacher. He had a school, and he had a student body. That was out white member was Jerry Ames. On -- see, because he took them out on tours, and they did some dances. You know, new dances, see, he was introducing. And he had to play these
commitments out. And so, that left us back on with -- we only had our composing tap dancer, John Rhythm Red. I called him (unintelligible). Debut John.

And he had a -- he composed a hit for us to do in the show which was "Got to go tap dancing tonight," which we still continue to convey, you see. And, see, he's not well now. And he's in intensive care, and we're trying to keep it going for his sake, and our choreographers' sake. Derby Wilson, he's away.
So, now -- well, so we finished a commitment down there. And see, then we come up and met Mr. Jack Bradley. And so, he wanted us to get into the hot jazz society, which was about musicians.
So, we began to tap dancing when they opened up a jazz museum up here in -- is that -- I think that's 55th Street near the Avenue of Americas.
